programs.title: NAVIGATING GLOBAL ECONOMIC CHANGE | Exclusive with WEF President
programs.desc: The year 2026 marks the 20th anniversary of the establishment of the World Economic Forum's Beijing Representative Office. CGTN's Guan Xin speaks with Alois Zwinggi, president and CEO of WEF, to look back on nearly five decades of cooperation between WEF and China, examine the future of globalization and explore how 'China Opportunity 2.0' can further advance global cooperation in supply chain resilience, green technology and AI governance.

programs.title: Tennis Australia exec on the Australian Open's China push
programs.desc: China is taking center court in the Australian Open's global growth strategy. The Grand Slam has kicked off its 2027 China campaign in Beijing, aiming to engage fans through localized digital content, live events, retail and Chinese cultural Ambassadors. Tennis Australia says its long-term investment is paying off, with China now one of the tournament's largest international markets.

programs.title: China-US partnerships fueling rapid growth
programs.desc: Starbucks landed in China when coffee was a novelty. Today, 1 in 5 stores globally is there. American fast food and retail giants placed the same bet, and cashed in. Now local brands are out-executing them. The fix? Partner with Chinese private equity. Here's why it's working, and what it means for both sides.

programs.title: The green bridge between China & US
programs.desc: In 2019, Tesla was running on fumes. Shanghai handed it a lifeline, a gigafactory built in 10 months. Today, that plant produces nearly half of all Teslas using 95% local parts. That same playbook is expanding across green tech, pairing Chinese battery tech with American software. When the world's two largest economies build together, clean energy gets cheaper and faster for everyone.

programs.title: Reforesting Iceland
programs.desc: The stark and austere landscape of Iceland is iconic and one of the most noticeable traits is a lack of trees. The Icelandic ecosystem is classified as one of the most degraded in Europe, having experienced one of the worst cases of deforestation in the world. When viking settlers first arrived in Iceland, the land was covered in birch forest. But after hundreds of years of sheep-grazing, soil erosion and eruptions, Iceland was left with just 0.5% forest cover and a big problem: how do you grow trees in one of Europe’s largest deserts? RAZPR's Gabrielle Lawrence heads to the remote corners of south Iceland to meet Samson Harearson and Hrefna Jensdóttir from Iceland's Land and Forest Service working on an ambitious project, to grow trees in a treeless land.

programs.title: RAZOR: Flower Power Mining
programs.desc: Every year, the world mines for billions of tonnes of metals. And the way we do it often comes at a huge cost to the environment. Nickel is one metal in huge demand as a vital component of electric vehicle batteries. One solution is blooming in an unexpected corner of the world in the form of a very special and unique plant called Odontarrhena decipiens. This is a type of hyperaccumulator, a plant which naturally takes up a large amount of certain metals, like nickel, from the soil. The plants are then processed to extract the nickel. The process, known as phytomining or agromining, is more efficient and less energy intensive, than traditional mining. RAZOR's Reya El-Salahi meets Professor Aida Bani, an instrumental part of Albanian phytomining research, who has dedicated two decades to studying this special type of plant. In Northern Albania a start-up is growing a stunning site of hyperaccumulator plants on a larger scale. Metalplant are cultivating 7 hectares with the aim of producing Nickel. They are also using enhanced rock weathering to make the process carbon negative.

programs.title: Integration and Empowerment - A New Paradigm of Sino-German Cooperation Driven by Technological Innovation
programs.desc: For the first time, the Sino-German Forum on Cooperation and Development of New Energy Vehicles and the VDA Round Table of Presidents/CEOs of German Suppliers in China will be jointly held as a combined event during the World New Energy Vehicle Congress (WNEVC). The forum brings together industry leaders to explore collaborative development in the NEV sector, covering topics such as industry trends, innovation, policy frameworks, and international cooperation.

programs.title: Architecture Intelligence: When a skyscraper goes deep
programs.desc: Beneath the bustling metropolises, there often exists an intricate underground network where access corridors and subway tracks intertwine. Have you ever wondered how it is possible to construct a skyscraper above metro lines without causing disruptions to the daily commute of thousands? Discover the answer in this clip from Tech It Out's documentary "Architecture Intelligence."

programs.title: Architecture Intelligence: Super bridge above the Yangtze
programs.desc: The mighty Yangzte poses a significant challenge for bridge builders. Let's witness how architects overcome this obstacle by constructing China's longest-spanning dual-purpose suspension bridge over this untamed river. Watch this clip of Tech It Out's documentary "Architecture Intelligence" for more.

programs.title: Meet China: From Little Toys to Global Factories, How Chinese Creativity Travels
programs.desc: In this episode of Meet China, we explore how “Made in China” is taking on new forms. A monster toy becomes a global collectible, an ocean park in southern China turns wonder into repeat visits, and a smart EV factory in Zhejiang shows how cars are built for overseas markets. In central China’s Xuchang, a small city supplies much of the world’s hair products, while in Guangxi, an Italian chef blends pizza with traditional medicinal food. From blind boxes to electric vehicles, wigs and a yam-and-lamb pizza, this episode reveals how Chinese creativity, scale and culture are reaching the world in unexpected ways.

programs.title: How China's ocean kingdom makes billions
programs.desc: In Southern China, a theme park you've likely never heard of is attracting more annual visitors than Hollywood Universal. The question is, how? Meet Chimelong Ocean Kingdom. It holds seven Guinness World Records and features the largest aquarium on earth. CGTN's Yu Hongyu dives into the strategy behind the splash to see how a local park created a hundred-billion-dollar opportunity.

programs.title: China's Kungfu theme park: A wild ride back in time
programs.desc: At Wansuishan Martial Arts City in central China’s Kaifeng, Henan Province, you’re not just a visitor - you’re part of the story. Every segment in the park is part of an immersive experience rooted in Chinese martial arts and traditional culture. From live matchmaking shows to iron flower performances, from Song Dynasty streets to interactive stages, this uniquely Chinese theme park – with not even one roller coaster or scary ride – was able to record over 24 million visits in 2025.

programs.title: Bizfocus: From myth to reality: How tech brings Eastern imagination to life
programs.desc: Ever wondered what China’s version of “Adam and Eve” or “Beauty and the Beast” looks like? While the world’s theme parks are all about Western fairy tales, one Chinese park took a different path—Fantawild brings ancient Eastern myths to life with mind-blowing tech and art. In this episode of Bizfocus, CGTN’s Xu Yi and her new friends from Pakistan and Bangladesh go for adventure in Fantawild Oriental Heritage in Mianyang, Sichuan. Gods, legends, and the tech behind the magic—all in one epic trip.

programs.title: BizTalk: China-US economic & trade watch
programs.desc: Global markets are closely watching the trajectory of China-US economic and trade ties. In this episode of BizTalk, CGTN's Michael Wang speaks with Jiang Wenran, founding director of the China Institute at the University of Alberta, and Lyu Xiang, research fellow at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences. They look ahead to how bilateral economic and trade ties could evolve over the next few years.

programs.title: The AI revolution is here - but are we ready for what comes next?
programs.desc: In this special joint episode of World Economic Forum and CGTN, hosts Robin Pomeroy from World Economic Forum and Guan Xin, CGTN Anchor, sit down with Professor Arun Sundararajan of New York University's Stern School of Business, a member of the WEF AI Governance Alliance and author of The Sharing Economy. They dive into the most pressing questions about artificial intelligence. From the future of employment to the deepening divide over AI governance and technological sovereignty, this conversation brings together perspectives from the US, China, and the global stage on how AI is reshaping economies, societies, and geopolitics.

programs.title: Highland industries, high-quality future
programs.desc: From smart ranching to vegetable greenhouses, from cold-chain logistics to cross-border trade… We take a look at Xizang's industrial transformation and see how the plateau is leaping into a new era of development.

programs.title: Discovering Guizhou: Miao culture extravaganza
programs.desc: What do spicy peppers, handmade guitars, and green cities have in common? Guizhou. In our new on-the-ground mini-series ChinaHorizons, we invite you to join our trip to Guizhou province. For the first stop, we record our podcast in a traditional Miao people's village cluster to appreciate diversified cultures, intangible cultural heritage items and delicious local cuisines.

programs.desc: Despite its fertile tropical landscape, Malaysia produces only around two-thirds of the rice it needs. Discover more in CGTN's special series #FarmedwithChina. #Chinavsionary

programs.title: Farmed with China: Vietnam's food trade levels up
programs.desc: How is Vietnam's cassava industry reaching global markets? With technical support and cross-border cooperation with China, one crop is moving up the value chain — from local farms to international supply chains.

programs.title: Farmed with China: Thailand's farms go high-tech
programs.desc: As labor grows scarce, how can the land still yield abundant harvests? China-Thailand cooperation is providing solutions: machines for farmers, jobs in factories, and training for young agricultural engineers. Technology is more than equipment — it brings efficiency and hope.

programs.title: Cambodia's rice prawn=making more money!
programs.desc: Rice and prawn grow better together. Prawn loosens the soil and control pests, while rice cleans and oxygenates the water. One field, two harvests. A team from Shanghai Ocean University brought this eco-farming model to Cambodia, helping turn rice paddies into new sources of income.

programs.title: Laos farmers hack one season into many
programs.desc: Laos is transforming traditional agriculture into a modern locally-adapted system with the cooperation of China, applying benefits from a decade of seed innovation as well as the domestic development of potash resources. Alongside China-Laos Railway strengthening the supply chain, grain production is also gaining a stronger foundation. Explore the story in CGTN's special series Farmed With China.

programs.title: Working as one: Three Chinese villages pool resources for shared growth
programs.desc: Three villages in Shandong run on one shared economic ledger. It is a rural experiment in resource re‑allocation, pointing to alternative possibilities for rural communities across the developing world. In this episode of BizFocus, CGTN anchor Lincoln Humphries explores three villages in Dezhou, Shandong for their stories.
